summary: Defines a Mobile IPv4 extension that carries a Network Access Identifier. When a mobile node moves between foreign networks and must be re-authenticated, the home AAA server may lack the information to do so correctly, and this extension supplies it.

eli5.summary: When you move to a new place, the new place needs to know who you are. This adds your name tag to the message so your home office can vouch for you.

questions: mobile ipv4 network access identifier extension
what is the mobile ip nai carrying extension
mobile ipv4 reauthentication between foreign networks
what is a home agent nai
subtitle: A Mobile IPv4 extension that lets a home agent hand a mobile node the identities of itself and its home AAA server.

tldr.problem: When a mobile node moves between foreign networks it must be re-authenticated, but a home network with several AAA servers and home agents may not know which home agent the session was assigned to.
tldr.mechanism: A new NAI Carrying Extension (type 136) lets the home agent put its own identity and its home AAA server's identity, as Network Access Identifiers, into a Registration Reply. The mobile node sends them back in later registration requests.
tldr.outcome: The new AAA server can route re-authentication to the right server and keep the same home agent. The extension is a Proposed Standard and is also open to other kinds of NAI later.

today: RFC 3846 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2004. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Identities Need to Travel
sections.content:
Networks often place several AAA (Authentication, Authorization and Accounting) servers in one home domain for redundancy. When a mobile node registers through a visited network, one of those home servers handles the authentication. When the node later moves to another visited domain it must authenticate again, and the RFC points out that it cannot be guaranteed the same home AAA server will handle it. The new server may not know which home agent (HA) the session was assigned to.

There is a second gap. A registration request normally carries only the home agent's IP address, as defined in RFC 3344. Some AAA systems, such as Diameter, use realm-based routing and need the home agent's fully qualified domain name (FQDN). A reverse DNS lookup would only reveal the identity of the Mobile IP interface, which may not match the home agent's FQDN.
sections.eli5: Imagine a school with many office staff. When you move to a new class, the new teacher does not know which office person handled your file. This gives you a note naming the right person.

sections.title: The NAI Carrying Extension
sections.content:
The NAI Carrying Extension can appear in Mobile IP Registration Request and Reply messages and in Agent Advertisements. Any node that wants to send identity information as a Network Access Identifier (NAI) may use it. The layout has four parts:

  • Type: 136, a skippable extension.
  • Length: an 8-bit unsigned integer that excludes the Type and Length fields. It MUST be set to 1 plus the total length of the NAI field.
  • Sub-Type: says what kind of NAI is carried.
  • NAI: the NAI as a string.

This document defines two subtypes. The RFC expects other documents to define more.
sections.eli5: It is a small labelled box added to a message. The label says what kind of name is inside, and the name itself is written as text.

sections.title: Where the Extension Goes and How It Is Used
sections.content:
When a mobile node or home agent adds the extension to a registration message, it MUST appear before any authentication extensions. A foreign agent that adds it must likewise place it before the authentication extensions the foreign agent adds.

If a home agent added the extension to a Registration Reply and does not see it in later Registration Requests from the mobile node, it can assume the node does not understand the extension. In that case the home agent SHOULD NOT add it to further replies.
sections.eli5: The name tag has to be stuck on before the signature stamp goes on. If you never show the tag back, the sender figures you cannot read it and stops sending it.

sections.title: The HA and AAAH Identity Subtypes
sections.content:
HA Identity is subtype 1. It holds the home agent's NAI in the form hostname@realm, which together make the FQDN hostname.realm. A home agent using it MUST include it in the first Registration Reply to a mobile node that is not currently registered. A mobile node that receives it MUST provide it in every later registration request when re-authentication is needed. If the node needs a specific home agent and has the NAI, it MUST include it in its initial registration request. Failure to re-authenticate, for instance because no AAAH can be reached, ends the Mobile IP session.

AAAH Identity is subtype 2. It holds the NAI of the home AAA server in the same form. When several AAA servers exist in the home network, a home agent that supports AAAH selection MUST provide it in the first Registration Reply. The mobile node SHOULD save the latest one and SHOULD send it in each re-authenticating request, for efficiency. If the indicated server cannot be reached, a new AAAH Identity is returned.

A foreign agent that receives either NAI in a registration request SHOULD include it when asking the AAA infrastructure to authenticate the node, if the AAA protocol can carry it.
sections.eli5: There are two name tags. One names the home agent and one names the home office server. You keep the latest ones and show them whenever you need to prove who you are again.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Mobile IP messages that carry this extension MUST be authenticated as described in RFC 2794, unless other authentication methods have been agreed upon. The RFC therefore says it does not lessen the security of Mobile IP messages.

The identities in the extension MAY be sent in the clear over the network. The authors do not envision that this information would create security issues.
sections.eli5: The name tags are not secret, like a name on a lunch box. The whole message is still checked so nobody can fake it.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC defines one new Mobile IP extension, type number 136, and a new sub-type numbering space in which values 1 and 2 are assigned. New sub-type numbers need Expert Review, and a specification is required.

The extension is not specific to AAA NAIs, so future NAIs outside that category may use the same sub-type space. The NAI Carrying Extension should get a value from both the IANA space for Mobile IPv4 skippable extensions and the space for Mobile IPv4 advertisement extensions, ideally the same value in each.
sections.eli5: IANA keeps the official list of numbers. This RFC asks for number 136 for the new box and sets aside a list of its own kinds, with 1 and 2 already taken.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: 1 plus the length of the NAI field.

items.label: HA Identity
items.desc: NAI of the home agent, as hostname@realm.

items.label: AAAH Identity
items.desc: NAI of the home AAA server, as hostname@realm.
